holidays.name: Pretend to Be a Time Traveler Day
holidays.description: Today you can act like you've just stepped out of a time machine. Wear a mix of eras, act baffled by ordinary gadgets, or tell strangers you're visiting from 2347. Keep a straight face for bonus points.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, playful observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular excuse for costumes, in-character conversations, and silly social media posts.
holidays.funFact: Physicist Stephen Hawking once threw a party for time travelers. He sent the invitations out only after the party was over, so that only people from the future could know about it. No one showed up.

holidays.name: National Brownie Day
holidays.description: This is a day to celebrate the fudgy, chewy, chocolatey square. Whether you like yours gooey in the middle, cakey, or loaded with nuts, today is the day to eat one without guilt.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance that honors the classic American chocolate dessert. It lands in the middle of the holiday baking season.
holidays.funFact: A popular legend says the brownie was born at the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago. It was supposedly created for women attending the fair who wanted a dessert smaller than a slice of cake that fit in a boxed lunch.

holidays.name: National Lard Day
holidays.description: This day is a salute to rendered pig fat, the old kitchen workhorse behind flaky pie crusts, tender biscuits, and crispy fried food. Bakers and traditional cooks use it today to show off a once-beloved ingredient.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a staple that dominated home kitchens for generations.
holidays.funFact: Lard has about half the saturated fat of butter by some measures and was a pantry essential long before vegetable shortening arrived. Many pastry chefs still swear it makes the flakiest pie crust.
